Let R be the positive’s exact rank among N eligible negatives plus itself, using a fixed total order (score descending, item ID ascending for ties). Exactly K=R−1 negatives precede it. With m unique uniformly sampled negatives, X∼Hypergeom(N,K,m), sampled rank r=1+X, E[r]=1+mK/N, Var(r)=m(K/N)(1−K/N)(N−m)/(N−1), and E[HR@10]=P(X≤9)=hypergeom.cdf(9,N,K,m). These are direct analytical checks requiring no fitted model; use each user’s actual eligible pool. Sampling with replacement instead gives a binomial law. [SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.hypergeom.html).

Recommended calibration: freeze scores and tie handling; construct nested candidates from prefixes of one random negative permutation. Sampled rank must never decrease as m grows, HR@10 must never increase, and m=N must reproduce exact rank and full-pool HR@10. Independently repeated permutations should reproduce the analytical rank mean and hit probability. For B repetitions, per-user hit-frequency Monte Carlo SE is √[p(1−p)/B]. Compare models on identical users and candidate draws; report paired differences, category-stratified paired user-bootstrap intervals, and separate uncertainty from candidate resampling versus user sampling. Preserve the pinned benchmark; perform these as validation diagnostics.

The exact title “On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems” could not be verified. The directly relevant [Krichene–Rendle paper](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establishes that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; bias corrections trade bias against variance. Subsequent [rank-distribution estimation research](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16537) develops broader corrections. Thus agreement with hypergeometric expectations validates sampling implementation, but cannot establish that sampled HR@10 preserves full-pool model ordering.
